## 工作要求

   不得删段、加速、倒放、冻结或用图片替代。输出时长与输入差异不超过 0.5 秒。

## 评分规则

最终分 S = 主体分 B × 质量系数 Q。

六段等权，每段主体分最高100/6（约16.67）。该段在实际旁白中识别错误、未给出物种或只在字幕/JSON写对时，该段主体分为0；不会因此清零其他正确片段。允许标准别名、明确的单一暂定识别；纯音频转写的同音字差异不作物种识别错误，不接受枚举候选碰答案。
B = (100/6) × Σ I_i × (0.40 + 0.32F_i + 0.28E_i)。I_i=物种识别正确1/否则0；F_i=科普事实准确性；E_i=解说与实际视听证据对应程度，F/E范围0–1。不要把一般物种习性说成片中发生的事件。视野不清时如实说明可得对应证据分。

Q = 0.70H + 0.20A + 0.10D，所有子项0–1，各章等权：
- H：自然韵律35%、音色舒适25%、发音清晰25%、语速停顿15%。重视实际人类听感。
- A：原声保留40%、混音平衡40%、至少2秒无旁白且有原声窗口20%。
- D：画面完整40%、字幕同步与可读30%、解说时机20%、交付有效10%。

全片无可播放成片或没有可懂中文旁白，Q=0。缺章、改速、时长误差超过0.5秒、缺少必需交付、任一章无中文解说或无原声窗口、替换伪造原声，均为硬性要求不通过。分数与硬性要求分开展示；通过需S≥80且全部门槛通过。评审无法判断时标记待评，不默认为满分。

只评实际成片，不用文稿、字幕或JSON代替声音证据。六段不保证六个不同物种。短章节可以简洁介绍，不能为了长篇科普挤掉原声窗口。

Luscinia megarhynchos juvénile sp. Luscinia megarhynchos The Common Nightingale is a fairly stout passerine, larger than the European Robin, whose general shape it shares. It is an unobtrusive bird and, were it not for its loud song in spring, it would readily go unnoticed. It is unobtrusive in its plumage too, a warm rufous-brown above. The most rufous parts are the crown, the wings, the rump, the uppertail-coverts and the tail, the latter recalling that of a redstart. A greyish tinge is frequent on the neck and the sides of the head. The large dark eye is ringed by a conspicuous creamy-white eye-ring. The bill is two-toned, brown above and pink over two-thirds of the lower mandible. The underparts are whitish, with a fairly well-marked rufous-brown band across the breast and flanks of the same hue. The undertail-coverts are rufous cream. The legs are sturdy and brownish to pinkish. Like all young muscicapids, the young Common Nightingale has a spotted plumage. In this species the spots are rufous cream and make it easy to tell from the adult. 3 subspecies are described. The most rufous is the western nominate subspecies megarhynchos, which is the one found in Europe. The eastern subspecies golzi has a less warm, greyer plumage. Similar species Thrush Nightingale Distribution ♂ adulte plum. nuptial sp. Luscinia megarhynchos adulte plum. internuptial sp. Luscinia megarhynchos The Common Nightingale is a Eurasian species which in the warmer months occupies a continuous geographical belt running from the Atlantic Ocean to western Mongolia, centred on temperate Europe as well as on western Asia at the same latitudes. In the north, only southern England is occupied, Scandinavia is not. In the south, it occupies the Maghreb. The African wintering range is a continuous sub-Sahelian belt running from Senegal in the west to Ethiopia, Somalia and Kenya in the east, taking in the countries bordering the Gulf of Guinea, Nigeria and the Central African Republic. Acrocephalus scirpaceus The Common Reed Warbler is the most common of our aquatic warblers, which are recognized by their sharp profile (Acrocephalus), round tail at the end, and long undertail coverts. It frequents reed beds with phragmites during the breeding season. Both sexes are identical. In fresh plumage, the adult has quite warm upper parts, a dark, muted brown. A clear russet tone is visible on the lower back, rump, and coverts. The front of the crown is slightly darker. The pale fringes of the remiges contrast with the dark centers of these, breaking the uniformity of the plumage. The primary projection is medium, about equal to 2/3 of the length of the tertiaries. The short, cream-russet eyebrow, clear in front of the eye, does not continue behind or is indistinct. It is highlighted by the front of the crown, a little darker than the rest and underlined by a dark loreal line. The eye is surrounded by a white eye ring broken in front and in the back. The lower parts are light. The flanks and sides of the chest are strongly infiltrated with chamois. The throat is white, a character that appears well when singing. The underside of the wings, the axillars and the undertail coverts are chamois-cream. The upper mandible is dark horn gray while the lower mandible is of a more or less vivid yellow. The legs are of a brownish colour and appear dark on the ground. The plant of the feet is dull yellow. The iris is light brown. In worn plumage (June-September for most birds), the adult upper parts become more grey-brown and the lower parts pale. The juvenile has much redder new plumage than the adult and its legs are greyer. It then looks very much like the other young reed warblers, Verderolle in particular, which can lead to confusion. Similar species Great Reed Warbler Basra Reed Warbler Manchurian Reed Warbler Greater Swamp Warbler Large-billed Reed Warbler Lesser Swamp Warbler Distribution adulte sp. Acrocephalus scirpaceus It is the most widespread warbler in Europe. It has a vast distribution area from the Atlantic in the west to the outer reaches of China in the east and from southern Scandinavia in the north to Iran in the south, touching on North Africa. Monotonous compared to that of other warblers, it consists of a long series of short syllables, which are scratched or whistled and repeated tirelessly with little variation. Some males (more talented than others?) occasionally improvise or introduce some imitations, especially in sympatry with the congener the Fan-tailed Warbler, but the Reed Warbler rhythm invariably reappears. Flight and movements ♂ adulte sp. Acrocephalus scirpaceus Low and relatively short flight. Behaviour and character adulte sp. Acrocephalus scirpaceus adulte plum. internuptial sp. Acrocephalus scirpaceus Common Reed Warbler pairs are territorial. Despite this, the density is often so high in reedbeds that the species is distributed almost semi-colonially. The male sings perched in sight in the upper part of a dry reed, while the female is busy with nesting activities. The birds move from stem to stem clinging to them sideways as all marshland passerines do, or else they take short flights from one massif to another. They move up and down agilely along the stems, going from one to the other in search of food. They are insectivorous, hunting insects in view in the wetlands or in the adjacent environments, such as crops or cleared land. When the song period is over, the only clues to their presence are the typical harsh cries of the Acrocephalus genus. It is also less linked to water and can be observed in different environments, including shrubs, where it betrays its presence with tec of anxiety, and sometimes with song strophes. The Common Reed Warbler is a great migrator that spends the boreal winter in sub-Saharan Africa south of the Sahara. It begins its migration at the end of August or the beginning of September. At this time, the young ones can fly well and have had enough time to gain enough weight to be able to make the big journey that awaits them. Our birds fly over the Mediterranean, then the arid regions of North Africa and finally reach the wet areas of sub-Saharan Africa, where they renew their worn plumage and find a lot of insects. This journey will take them about two months. Two months later, they'll already have to think about the return journey that will bring them back to Europe in mid-April. The adults return to the same nesting site each year, while the young ones are less loyal and ensure a genetic mix of the population. Habitat adulte sp. Acrocephalus scirpaceus ♂ adulte sp. Acrocephalus scirpaceus The Common Reed Warbler is a resident of the flooded Phragmites that borders still or flowing water, or invades marshy areas. Other faces such as Scirpus or Typha are less prized. The dry reed bed can also be occupied if the bird has no choice. Willows are tolerated but not essential. The reeds often form dense clumps where large animals find it difficult to penetrate, providing the birds with protection from many terrestrial predators. In some parts of Europe, the Common Reed Warbler has adapted to arable crops and built its nest there, but this remains rare. At the time of raising the young, adults can go to the adjacent grassland, cultivated or uncultivated, to find food. On migration, Reed Warblers can be observed in shrub and even tree habitats depending on the circumstances and resources. 声音和画面的处理

保留原始立体声的时间位置，只施加逐章增益、旁白期间的平滑音量避让和瞬时峰值限制。旁白目标综合响度为−18.5 LUFS；原声窗口及增益参数见 `mix_settings.json`。不加音乐，不使用参考鸟叫，不移动、复制或替换任何原始叫声。每章安排多处至少2秒的无旁白原声窗口，已检查其中独立旁白采样精确为零。

分析限制

本环境没有原生听音工具，未亲耳试听输入、参考录音或合成旁白。实际读取PCM采样，计算RMS和峰值，查看整体与局部声谱，结合画面代表帧和开喙动作判断。独立参考只做手工声谱观察，没有ASR、鸟声识别模型、其他识别模型、子代理、反向搜图或音视频指纹。配音听感没有人工听审；通过稳定音色、原生语速、语音时长、波形和词级时间戳作有限质量核验。
